claim: Huguet et al. 2025 provide source-specific indoor staff-location and movement-measurement context, not a route-choice calibration dataset. The study records timestamped UWB tag coordinates in one ED and describes hourly walking distance as Euclidean (straight-line) distances between locations of the same tag, aggregated per hour in metres. Its reported location-sequence and hex-grid analyses use time spent in floor-plan cells to classify staff type; expert-defined areas describe activity semantics and include a mixed-use corridor. In the route-relevant methods and results examined (paragraphs 12, 16–20, 23 and 40), the source does not specify individual route decisions, decision-time reachable alternatives, a complete choice set, selected path samples, movement purpose per path, graph revision/access constraints, or route interruptions. Hourly Euclidean displacement is not an obstacle-constrained route, route length, or route preference. Therefore route connectivity/access and reachable alternatives remain unknown; no route-preference coefficient, distribution, heuristic or generic default is supported. The reported measurements must not be interpreted as ED-generic policy.

primary_source.population: Consenting healthcare professionals wearing anonymized UWB tags at Le Corbusier Hospital emergency department, Firminy, France. This is a staff-location study; the route-choice record does not treat its participants as patients.
primary_source.period: 7 March to 21 April 2022; one emergency department.
primary_source.units: Timestamped positions were collected five times per second. The separately reported distance metric is hourly aggregated same-tag Euclidean displacement in metres. No route length or route-choice unit is reported.
